source: make a 3d game where you are an army soldier and your job is to damage all of the targets/robloxians and the more damages you get the more money you earn. use money to buy more guns and make the map look like a no man's land. make the map 1K studs wide and long.

image_prompt.text: Ruined structures on the battlefield that can be entered from outside and fought through
Target dummies and Robloxian figures standing across the battlefield to be shot at
A barren no man's land - churned mud, shell craters, wire and wreckage, nothing intact

layout_placement.text: A play boundary that contracts over the match, compressing players toward a shifting centre
Weapons distributed across the map so players arm themselves from the world

notes: The prompt answered the shape itself - a 1000x1000 no man's land is an open battlefield - so the preset was picked to match that shape rather than the mode. Its battle-royale mode options fight the prompt; see preset_rejected.
The map size is stated exactly at 1000 studs square, which the district scale band does not carry.
Guns are bought with money earned from damage dealt; there is no field for that economy.

open_questions.ask: Is there an end - a damage target, a round timer - or does it run forever?
Are the Robloxians static dummies on a range, or hostile NPCs that shoot back?
Is 1000x1000 the playable area or the whole plot including the border?

theme: Post-Apocalyptic - a WWI-style no man's land, muted and war-torn

coverage_missing.ask: What ends a session, if anything?
Do the targets fight back, or is this a range?
Should the gun shop be a place you walk to on the map, or just a purchase?

answers.ask: Is there an end - a damage target, a round timer - or does it run forever?
answers.answer: It runs continuously with no round timer or final damage target; players keep earning money by dealing damage and buying guns.

answers.ask: Are the Robloxians static dummies on a range, or hostile NPCs that shoot back?
answers.answer: Use hostile Robloxian NPCs that shoot back, fitting the army soldier no-man's-land setting.

answers.ask: Is 1000x1000 the playable area or the whole plot including the border?
answers.answer: The 1000x1000 studs is the playable no-man's-land area; keep any border or invisible limits outside or at its edge.
